content: The matching of contractors with projects according to their capabilities has been a consistent pattern in the industry, serving as the cornerstone of procurement and tender dynamics in the South African engineering sector [1, 2]. The financial parameters defining these capabilities are clearly delineated by the maximum tender values associated with each specific grade. An analysis of the maximum tender values by grade in South Africa demonstrates a distinct, overall increasing trend that aligns with the escalating complexity and capital requirements of larger engineering projects. At the lower end of the spectrum, Grade 2 permits a maximum tender value of 1.0 Million ZAR, accommodating smaller-scale projects and emerging contractors. As the grades progress, the financial thresholds expand significantly, culminating in a maximum tender value of 200.0 Million ZAR for Grade 8. This structured financial stratification ensures that contractors are only permitted to bid on projects that fall within their proven financial bandwidth, thereby safeguarding clients against the potential of contractor default and ensuring that structural steel and general engineering projects are adequately capitalized from inception to completion. Platforms dedicated to procurement, such as Simpletender and EasyTenders, are primarily engineered to facilitate current bidding opportunities rather than to serve as comprehensive repositories of historical data [1, 2]. Consequently, these platforms overwhelmingly reference present and upcoming tenders, including those requiring specific designations such as 2EP or 2ME grading, as well as various civil engineering projects [1, 2]. They fail to provide substantial insights into the historical tender activity of the 2020 to 2024 timeframe [1, 2]. This limitation is similarly reflected on the official Construction Industry Development Board website, where the designated section for current tenders is explicitly designed to display active opportunities for ongoing and future bidding, lacking a systematic archive of past tenders [40] . As a result, the platform remains a limited resource for addressing retrospective research queries concerning the evolution of contractor grading and historical tender activity [40] .
